The test only verifies an exception is thrown (superficial assertion) and does not assert multiple properties of returned objects or structure. Only one effective assertion path exists, so it is unlikely to detect subtle faults.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods in the visible code; the test is active and runnable.
No annotations or Javadoc comments link the test to a requirement ID or ticket. The code lacks traceability metadata per the evaluation criteria.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: This is a unit test focused on functional behavior. No performance or security tests are expected in this context and none are present; per the decision rules this practice is usually not-applicable for unit tests.
The method name 'test8' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected result. Decision rules mark generic names as non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: There are strong signs of automated test generation (EvoRunner, EvoAssertions, numeric test method name). The presence of autogenerated naming and EvoSuite runner indicates heavy code generation patterns, which matches the non-compliant indicators.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test appears to be a single minimal exceptional-case check without Given-When-Then structure or evidence of thoughtful design; per decision rules this is non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only interacts with public APIs (constructor, copia, retiraMax) and does not use reflection or inspect internal private state, meeting the criteria for maintainable behavior-focused tests.
Assertions in the test are minimal (fail inside try/catch) and lack descriptive messages or multiple specific assertions. Per rules, preference for specific assertions with messages is not met.
There are no commented-out tests or excessive inline comments. The only comment present documents expected exception message absence which is minimal and not obstructive.
The test does not use any sources of non-determinism (no Random, time-based calls, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies). It uses local state only, so it is deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test does not create files, databases, or modify static/global state. It only uses local variables and in-memory structures, so there are no persistent side effects requiring cleanup.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: No @Category/@Tag annotations are applied to the test or class. Although a UnitTest marker interface exists, it is not used via @Category on the test, so categorization is absent.

The test contains multiple distinct method calls on the SUT (fPHeapMax0.copia(...) and fPHeapMax0.constroi()). These represent more than one operation being exercised in the method, violating a single-Act/Assert focus.
The test uses only local variables and does not rely on shared mutable state or test execution order. No @Before/@After setup is required by evidence in this method.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only one test method is present in the provided class and it exercises an exceptional flow. There is no evidence of complementary happy-path tests for the same functionality.
Test data uses typical sizes (1006, array length 9). There is no evidence of boundary checks (zero, negative, max values, empty arrays) in this test method.
The test is self-contained and there is no duplicated logic across multiple test methods (only one test exists). Although no helpers/constants are present, the single short test avoids duplication.
